purpose: Reusable workflow from target spectrum to physical mechanism, structure choice, simulation, validation, and experience update.

pipeline.notes: Do not lock wavelength range to 0.9-1.7 um. Choose source band around the target mechanism and expected material response.

ranking_logic: Need very narrow isolated upward peak -> prefer quasi-BIC, defect cavity, or EIT-like bright-dark coupling.
Need extremely clean broad stopband background -> prefer DBR defect, metal shield plus aperture, or guided-mode resonance with background suppression.
Need tunable center wavelength by geometry -> prefer WGM/ring, photonic crystal defect, DBR cavity, or guided-mode resonance.
Need low loss and T<=1 strict energy -> avoid excessive metal absorption or direct metal aperture normalization artifacts.

selection_rules: quasi-BIC -> high-symmetry parent plus controlled symmetry breaking
DBR defect -> multilayer mirror plus half-wave or multi-order defect
EIT-like -> bright resonator plus weakly radiating dark resonator
guided-mode resonance -> periodic grating/slab mode phase matching
WGM -> ring/disk/radial cavity with weak coupling aperture

formula_examples: critical coupling: peak coupling optimized when external loss balances intrinsic plus other leakage

hard_rules: Only one real FDTD process at a time.
Use one spectrum monitor for transmission validation runs.
Use one field monitor for field validation runs.
Keep every original .fsp and result artifact.

pipeline.rule: Confirmed experience gets high weight only after convergence and field cross-check. Suspicious correlations remain low weight.
